This image is AC-DC Power Converter。An AC-DC power converter is a device that takes an AC input voltage and converts it to a DC output voltage. It can be used to step up the voltage or step down the voltage. The output voltage can be regulated to maintain a constant voltage. AC-DC power converters are commonly used in power supplies for electronic devices, such as computers, televisions, and portable audio equipment.
There are several types of AC-DC power converters, including linear power converters, switching power converters, and hybrid power converters. Linear power converters use a transformer to step up or step down the voltage, and then a rectifier to convert the AC voltage to DC. Switching power converters use a switch to step up or step down the voltage, and then a rectifier to convert the AC voltage to DC. Hybrid power converters use a combination of both linear and switching techniques to achieve the desired voltage conversion.
AC-DC power converters can be designed to be efficient, which means that they can convert a high percentage of the input power to the output power. This is achieved by using a low-resistance transformer, a low-resistance rectifier, and a high-resistance filter.
